Amplitude

Phase

dublinCore.description: Template MicroSim demo: plots the sinusoid x(t) = A sin(2 pi t / T + phi) over a 20 ms window next to its zero-phase reference, with sliders for amplitude, period and phase and an optional button that plays the same sinusoid as a tone at f = 1/T.
relation: Chapter 2: Introduction to Signals and Systems

learningObjectives: Calculate the frequency f = 1/T of a sinusoid from its period, and the number of cycles in a given time window
Calculate the starting value x(0) = A sin(phi) for a given amplitude and phase
Explain a phase phi as a time shift of phi T / 2 pi and identify a positive phase as a lead
Distinguish the audible effects of amplitude (loudness) and frequency (pitch) from the inaudible constant phase of a steady tone
prerequisites: Sine and cosine in radians and degrees
Time in milliseconds and frequency in hertz
Reading a function plotted against time

misconceptions.misconception: A positive phase delays the signal
misconceptions.correction: A sin(2 pi t / T + phi) = A sin(2 pi (t + phi T / 2 pi) / T), so a positive phase shifts the curve to the left: it is a lead
misconceptions.evidence: With T = 5.0 ms and phi = 90 degrees the blue curve peaks at t = 0, 1.25 ms before the gray zero-phase reference

misconceptions.misconception: A longer period means a higher pitch
misconceptions.correction: Period and frequency are reciprocals, f = 1/T
misconceptions.evidence: Increasing T from 2.5 ms to 10.0 ms lowers the readout from 400.0 Hz to 100.0 Hz and the tone drops two octaves

accessibility.screenReaderScript: A plot of the sinusoid x(t) = A sin(2 pi t / T + phi) in blue over a 20 millisecond window, with the zero-phase reference as a dashed gray line and a gold dot at x(0). Sliders set the amplitude A, the period T in milliseconds and the phase phi in degrees; a button plays the sinusoid as a tone at f = 1/T.

controls.label: Amplitude A
controls.description: Sets the peak value A of the sinusoid and the loudness of the tone

controls.label: Period T
controls.description: Sets the period T in milliseconds; the readout shows the frequency f = 1/T in hertz

controls.label: Phase φ
controls.description: Sets the phase phi in degrees; the readout shows phi in radians and x(0) = A sin(phi)

controls.label: Play Tone / Stop Tone
controls.description: Optional audio: starts and stops a sine tone at f = 1/T with amplitude 0.15 A (at most 0.3)

visualElements.description: Time plot of x(t) (blue) and the zero-phase reference (dashed gray) from 0 to 20 ms, with a gold dot at x(0) and a legend below the plot
Readout of f = 1/T in hertz, phi in radians and x(0), plus the tone status next to the button

model.description: Evaluates x(t) = A sin(2 pi t / T + phi) once per pixel column over 0 to 20 ms; the optional tone is a p5.Oscillator sine at f = 1/T
equations: x(t) = A sin(2 pi t / T + phi)

instructionalStrategies: Compare the curve with the zero-phase reference
extensions: Add a second sinusoid and plot the sum to show constructive and destructive interference
